title: SkillsBench: Benchmarking How Well Agent Skills Work Across Diverse Tasks
locator: Sections 3–6; Appendices F, J, K, N
claim: Curated packages improved selected terminal tasks; group comparisons by size/count are not controlled same-skill rewrites.
limitations: Task selection and harness-bundled skills limit generalization; no local reproduction.

title: SWE-Skills-Bench: Do Agent Skills Actually Help in Real-World Software Engineering?
locator: Sections 3.1–3.4, 4.2, 5; Appendix A
claim: Explicit invocation isolates post-activation utility; target-derived requirements and one run per cell constrain interpretation.
context: 98 skills, ten requirements each, four configurations.
limitations: Paper reports skill cleanup; independent code review confirms repo .claude cleanup and target staging, not exhaustive isolation; no contamination demonstrated.

title: OpenSkillEval: Automatically Auditing the Open Skill Ecosystem for LLM Agents
locator: Sections 2.1–2.3, 3.3, 4; Appendix A.2/A.4
claim: Artifact evaluation combines VLM judgments with interaction/data checks and validates score/rationale reasonableness on a human subset.
limitations: Award-site selection and same-rubric validation do not establish broad design/usability validity.

title: A Framework for Evaluating Agentic Skills at Scale
locator: Sections 2, 3, 4, 5.1, 6 Limitations
claim: Instruction-following and goal completion are separate; skill relevance is disclosed and hard-to-reproduce environments excluded.
limitations: Skill-derived task/rubric construction favors opinionated adherence; creative claims weakly supported.

title: Evaluating Skills, Not Just Agents: Agentic Continuous Evaluation of Skills
locator: Sections 4.3, 4.7–4.8, 6, 7; Appendices A/B/D
claim: Static scans differ from live behavior; composite lift mixes process and outcome; scorer contract matters.
context: 145 scan corpus; 947 paired cases in live subset.
limitations: Uneven coverage, internal skills, uncalibrated live judges, older accuracy criterion; no aggregate rescoring.

title: One Skill Too Many: How Co-Installed Skills Conflict in Coding Agents
locator: Sections 2.2, 3.6–3.10, 4, 6; Figure 1
claim: Completion can remain stable while expected exclusive behaviors disappear under co-installation.
context: Real public pairs; main Claude Code design and additional platform check.
limitations: Most individual cells single-run; extracted core functions and public installation reconstruction limit coverage.

title: One Skill Takes Over: Clashing Agent Skills and a One-File Fix
locator: Sections 3–5, 7; Appendices A/F
claim: Worked examples can drive takeover of compatible rules; correct joint examples help in this controlled setup.
context: 16 synthetic same-job pairs; both bodies injected.
limitations: Does not test natural discovery; formal rule fidelity is not broad artifact quality.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
locator: Sections 2.2–2.3, 3.3–3.4, 4; Tables 2–4
claim: Position and repetitive-list biases occur; the authors explicitly limit self-preference inference.
context: Conversational responses and older judge generations.
limitations: Agreement rates and mitigation efficacy are population/model-specific.

title: Length-Controlled AlpacaEval: A Simple Way to Debias Automatic Evaluators
locator: Sections 2–4, regression model and silver-standard discussion
claim: Length control reduces one evaluative confound; human preference is treated as a silver standard.
limitations: Does not validate equal-length artifacts or arbitrary design/writing judges.

title: Judging the Judges: A Systematic Evaluation of Bias Mitigation Strategies in LLM-as-a-Judge Pipelines
locator: Sections 3.1–3.5, 4; controlled-pair assumptions
claim: Bias mitigation and style effects depend on prompts, pair construction, aggregation, and model.
context: Five judges; benchmark and controlled synthetic pairs.
limitations: Claimed semantic equivalence/tie labels are assumptions; not design-user validation.

title: Reliability without Validity: A Systematic, Large-Scale Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge Models Across Agreement, Consistency, and Bias
locator: Sections 2.1, 3, 4.7–4.8, 5; limitations
claim: Stable repeated judgments can remain biased; small measured verbosity association is rubric-specific.
limitations: A selected rubric and benchmark set cannot establish universal judge validity.

title: Agent Skills specification
locator: Frontmatter table; body; progressive disclosure; validation
claim: Name and description are required; auxiliary fields/resources are optional; metadata, body and resources load at different stages.
limitations: Format validity does not establish usefulness; client behavior can differ.

title: Evaluating skill output quality
locator: Running evals; assertions; human review; analyzing patterns

limitations: Pushy descriptions can trade precision for recall; validation repeatedly used for selection is not untouched testing.
